summary: The committee accepted the consent agenda [24:37] before opening public comment [31:30], where speakers addressed curriculum content standards [32:02], educator workload and support [35:56], religious holiday policies [46:08], and ninth-grade course leveling [52:43]. District administrators presented annual school plans and performance metrics for Driscoll School [59:42] and Ridley School [1:34:32], highlighting tiered instructional strategies, literacy programs, and MCAS performance data. High school staff and leadership then presented a multi-year review of the World History Support Program (WISP) [2:00:57], examining enrollment statistics [2:09:05] and course structure options [2:35:01], which led to extensive committee discussion and staff statements regarding course tracking, academic rigor, and educator autonomy [2:46:00]. Additionally, officials reviewed districtwide enrollment projections and high school class sectioning [3:55:31], received brief subcommittee reports [4:35:35], and discussed potential future business regarding School Resource Officers and translation services [4:38:14] before voting to adjourn into executive session [4:41:48].
